openItems.explanation: FA-2501 equipment trailer, 20-ton tilt deck, $24,600.00: purchase order PO-24-117 was signed December 18, 2024 and the trailer was placed in service January 27, 2025. Property acquired before January 20, 2025 gets the 40% allowance, so the draft deducts $12,792.00; the depreciation software took 100%, $24,600.00, $11,808.00 more. A person confirms the purchase order was a binding written contract on that date and corrects the register before filing Form 4562.

The members' written consent approving 2025 officer pay ($290,000.00: salaries of $150,000.00 and $110,000.00 and the President's $30,000.00 bonus) was prepared December 18, 2025 and neither member has signed it. The draft deducts the $260,000.00 of salaries paid in 2025 on line 12 and Form 1125-E; the bonus, accrued to a 60% owner and paid January 9, 2026, is deducted in 2026 under section 267(a)(2). A person obtains the signed consent and support that the pay is reasonable.

On June 30, 2025 HANGS wired $120,000.00 to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC, a single-member LLC owned by the Vice President (a 40% member), with no note, no interest and no repayment date. The draft carries it as a receivable on Schedule L line 6 and imputes no interest. A person decides whether it is bona fide debt (a signed note at a market rate with a repayment schedule) or a distribution to the Vice President, and whether section 7872 interest applies.

The third installment, due September 15, 2025, was $7,075.00 short; the December 15 payment made it up. The regular method gives a $123.47 penalty, entered on line 34. A person decides whether the annualized income installment method (Form 2220 Schedule A) lowers it, and whether to attach Form 2220 or let the IRS bill the penalty.

Unsigned draft. The 2025 return and the $11,125.80 balance were due April 15, 2026; Form 7004 extends only the time to file, to October 15, 2026. Resolve BONUS-01, OFFICER-01 and RELATED-01 first; an officer signs, and a person files. $4,623.11 of contributions carries over to 2026. Nothing has been filed.

rules.question: What is the 2025 corporate income tax rate?
rules.whyItMatters: Schedule J line 1a is a flat 21% of taxable income; there are no brackets.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), Schedule J, line 1a.
rules.excerpt: Line 1a. Income tax. Multiply taxable income (page 1, line 30) by 21% (0.21). Enter this amount on line 1a.
matchPhrases: multiply taxable income (page 1, line 30) by 21% (0.21)
rules.ruleOrLimit: Income tax is 21% of taxable income.
rules.hangsApplication: Taxable income of $282,392.05 times 21% is $59,302.33, the total tax on line 31. There are no credits and no corporate alternative minimum tax (that applies only to very large corporations).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: When is the 2025 calendar-year return due?
rules.whyItMatters: A calendar-year corporation files and pays by the 15th day of the 4th month after its year ends.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), When To File.
rules.excerpt: Generally, a corporation must file its income tax return by the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of its tax year.
matchPhrases: generally, a corporation must file its income tax return by the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of its tax year
rules.ruleOrLimit: Due April 15, 2026 for a calendar 2025 year; Form 7004 extends the time to file, not to pay.
rules.hangsApplication: The return and the $11,125.80 balance (tax less payments, plus the estimated tax penalty) were due April 15, 2026. This run prepares an unsigned draft; a person confirms the filing status, signs and files (RETURN-01).
rules.unresolved: A person reviews, signs and files (RETURN-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: Must HANGS complete Schedules L, M-1 and M-2, and is Schedule M-3 needed instead?
rules.whyItMatters: Small corporations may skip the balance sheet and reconciliations; corporations with $10 million of assets file Schedule M-3 instead of M-1.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), Schedule L and Schedule M-1.
rules.excerpt: Corporations with total receipts (page 1, line 1a plus lines 4 through 10) and total assets at the end of the tax year less than $250,000 are not required to complete Schedules L, M-1, and M-2 ... Corporations with total assets nonconsolidated ... of $10 million or more on the last day of the tax year must file Schedule M-3 (Form 1120) instead of Schedule M-1.
matchPhrases: corporations with total receipts (page 1, line 1a plus lines 4 through 10) and total assets at the end of the tax year less than $250,000 are not required to complete schedules l, m-1, and m-2
of $10 million or more on the last day of the tax year must file schedule m-3 (form 1120) instead of schedule m-1
rules.pageOrSection: Schedule L, Balance Sheets per Books; Schedule M-1
rules.ruleOrLimit: Schedules L, M-1 and M-2 are required at $250,000 of receipts or assets; Schedule M-3 replaces M-1 at $10 million of assets.
rules.hangsApplication: Total receipts of $5,315,812.58 and year-end assets well over $250,000 but under $10 million: Schedules L, M-1 and M-2 are completed and Schedule M-3 is not required.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: Is Form 1125-E required, and what supports the officers' 2025 pay?
rules.whyItMatters: At $500,000 of total receipts, officer pay is reported officer by officer on Form 1125-E; the pay must be approved and reasonable.
rules.excerpt: If the corporation's total receipts (line 1a, plus lines 4 through 10) are $500,000 or more, complete Form 1125-E, Compensation of Officers. Enter on Form 1120, line 12, the amount from Form 1125-E, line 4.
matchPhrases: if the corporation's total receipts (line 1a, plus lines 4 through 10) are $500,000 or more, complete form 1125-e, compensation of officers
rules.ruleOrLimit: Form 1125-E is attached when total receipts are $500,000 or more.
rules.hangsApplication: Form 1125-E is required. The salaries paid in 2025, $150,000.00 to the President and $110,000.00 to the Vice President, agree with payroll and the ledger. The members' written consent approving 2025 pay, the $30,000.00 bonus included, was prepared December 18, 2025 and is unsigned (OFFICER-01).
rules.unresolved: A person obtains the signed consent and support that the pay is reasonable (OFFICER-01).

rules.question: Can the bonus accrued at December 31, 2025 to the President, a 60% owner, be deducted in 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: An accrual-method corporation deducts an amount owed to a cash-method related person only when that person includes it in income; an individual owning more than 50% is related.
rules.excerpt: (2) Matching of deduction and payee income item in the case of expenses and interest ... any deduction allowable under this chapter in respect of such amount shall be allowable as of the day as of which such amount is includible in the gross income of the person to whom the payment is made ... (2) an individual and a corporation more than 50 percent in value of the outstanding stock of which is owned, directly or indirectly, by or for such individual;
matchPhrases: matching of deduction and payee income item in the case of expenses and interest

any deduction allowable under this chapter in respect of such amount shall be allowable as of the day as of which such amount is includible in the gross income of the person to whom the payment is made
(2) an individual and a corporation more than 50 percent in value of the outstanding stock of which is owned, directly or indirectly, by or for such individual
rules.ruleOrLimit: Accrued pay to a more-than-50% owner is deductible in the year the owner is paid.
rules.hangsApplication: The $30,000.00 bonus accrued December 31, 2025 to the President (60%) was paid January 9, 2026. It is deducted on the 2026 return, not on 2025's: line 12 is $260,000.00 and the $30,000.00 is added back on Schedule M-1 line 5.
rules.sourceTitle: 26 U.S. Code 267, Losses, expenses, and interest with respect to transactions between related taxpayers

rules.question: How much of the 2025 meals and entertainment account is deductible?
rules.whyItMatters: Business meals are 50% deductible; entertainment is not deductible at all.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), line 26, Travel, meals, and entertainment.
rules.excerpt: Generally, entertainment expenses, membership dues, and facilities used in connection with these activities cannot be deducted. ... Generally, the corporation can deduct only 50% of the amount otherwise allowable for non-entertainment-related meal expenses paid or incurred in its trade or business.
matchPhrases: generally, entertainment expenses, membership dues, and facilities used in connection with these activities cannot be deducted
generally, the corporation can deduct only 50% of the amount otherwise allowable for non-entertainment-related meal expenses paid or incurred in its trade or business
rules.pageOrSection: Line 26. Other Deductions: Travel, meals, and entertainment
rules.hangsApplication: Account 6350 holds $21,640.00: $19,800.00 of business meals, deductible at 50% ($9,900.00), and $1,840.00 of stadium suite tickets, entertainment with no meal, not deductible. $11,740.00 goes on Schedule M-1 line 5c.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: Is the Labor and Industries citation penalty deductible?
rules.whyItMatters: Fines and penalties paid to a government for violating a law are not deductible, apart from restitution and costs of coming into compliance.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), line 26, Fines or similar penalties.
rules.excerpt: Generally, no deduction is allowed for fines or similar penalties paid or incurred to, or at the direction of, a government or governmental entity for violating any law, or for the investigation or inquiry into the potential violation of a law, except: amounts that constitute restitution or remediation of property, amounts paid to come into compliance with the law ...
matchPhrases: generally, no deduction is allowed for fines or similar penalties paid or incurred to, or at the direction of, a government or governmental entity for violating any law
rules.pageOrSection: Line 26. Other Deductions: Fines or similar penalties
rules.ruleOrLimit: Government fines and penalties are not deductible.
rules.hangsApplication: The $4,250.00 fall-protection citation penalty paid July 14, 2025 sits in account 6500, taxes and licenses. It is taken out of line 17 and added back on Schedule M-1 line 5. Nothing in the file shows any part as restitution or compliance cost.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: How much of the $36,000.00 of contributions is deductible for 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: A corporation deducts contributions only up to 10% of its taxable income figured before the contributions; the rest carries over for 5 years.
rules.excerpt: Generally, the total amount claimed cannot be more than 10% of taxable income (line 30) computed without regard to the following. Any deduction for contributions. ... Charitable contributions over the 10% limitation cannot be deducted for the tax year but can be carried over to the next 5 tax years.
matchPhrases: generally, the total amount claimed cannot be more than 10% of taxable income (line 30) computed without regard to the following
charitable contributions over the 10% limitation cannot be deducted for the tax year but can be carried over to the next 5 tax years
rules.pageOrSection: Line 19. Charitable Contributions: Limitation on deduction; Carryover
rules.ruleOrLimit: Limit: 10% of taxable income before the contributions deduction; the excess carries forward 5 years.
rules.hangsApplication: Taxable income before contributions is $313,768.94, so the limit is $31,376.89. Of the $36,000.00 given to four section 501(c)(3) organizations, $31,376.89 is deducted on line 19 and $4,623.11 carries over to 2026 through 2030 (Schedule M-1 line 5b). There was no carryover from 2024.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: Is the increase in the allowance for doubtful accounts deductible?
rules.whyItMatters: The return deducts debts that became worthless during the year, not additions to a book reserve.
rules.excerpt: Line 15. Bad debts. Enter the total debts that became worthless in whole or in part during the tax year.
matchPhrases: enter the total debts that became worthless in whole or in part during the tax year
rules.ruleOrLimit: Deduct debts that became worthless in the year.
rules.hangsApplication: No receivable was written off in 2025; the $2,180.00 book expense raised the allowance from $4,000.00 to $6,180.00. Line 15 is zero and the $2,180.00 is added back on Schedule M-1 line 5.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 1120 (2025), U.S. Corporation Income Tax Return

rules.question: What special depreciation allowance applies to the excavator, the crew 3 truck and the tablets acquired in 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act restored the 100% special allowance for qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 4562 (2025), What's New and line 14.
rules.excerpt: P.L. 119-21, commonly known as the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, reinstated the 100% special depreciation allowance for certain qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025 ... However, you can elect to take a 40% special depreciation allowance ... during first tax year ending after January 19, 2025, instead of taking the 100% special depreciation allowance.
matchPhrases: reinstated the 100% special depreciation allowance for certain qualified property acquired and placed in service after january 19, 2025

however, you can elect to take a 40% special depreciation allowance (60% for long production period property and certain aircraft) for this property during first tax year ending after january 19, 2025
rules.pageOrSection: What's New: Special depreciation allowance for certain qualified property acquired after January 19, 2025
rules.ruleOrLimit: 100% for qualified property acquired and placed in service after January 19, 2025, unless the 40% election or an election out is made.
rules.hangsApplication: FA-2502 excavator ($186,000.00, contract February 24, 2025), FA-2503 crew 3 truck ($62,400.00) and FA-2504 tablets ($15,800.00): 100%, $264,200.00. The client made no election out and no 40% election (Q9).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 4562 (2025), Depreciation and Amortization

rules.question: What allowance applies to the trailer ordered in December 2024 and delivered in January 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: Property acquired before January 20, 2025 and placed in service in 2025 keeps the phased-down 40% allowance; the acquisition date is the binding contract date, not the delivery.
rules.effective: Publication 946 (2025), chapter 3, Certain qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017, and before January 20, 2025.
rules.excerpt: Unless you elect out, you must take a 40% special depreciation allowance for certain qualified property acquired after September 27, 2017, and placed in service after December 31, 2024, and before January 1, 2026 (other than certain property with a long production period and certain aircraft).
matchPhrases: unless you elect out, you must take a 40% special depreciation allowance for certain qualified property acquired after september 27, 2017, and placed in service after december 31, 2024, and before january 1, 2026
rules.ruleOrLimit: 40% for qualified property acquired before January 20, 2025 and placed in service in 2025.
rules.hangsApplication: FA-2501 trailer, $24,600.00: purchase order PO-24-117 signed December 18, 2024, delivered January 27, 2025. The allowance is 40%, $9,840.00, plus 20% MACRS on the $14,760.00 left, $2,952.00: $12,792.00. The client's register took 100% ($24,600.00), $11,808.00 too much. The draft uses $12,792.00 (BONUS-01).
rules.unresolved: A person confirms PO-24-117 was a binding written contract on December 18, 2024 and corrects the register (BONUS-01).

rules.question: What did HANGS have to pay in each 2025 installment?
rules.whyItMatters: Each installment is 25% of the smaller of the 2025 tax and the 2024 tax (from a full 12-month return showing tax); a large corporation can use last year's tax only for its first installment.
rules.effective: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty; Part II line 8; Part III line 9.
rules.excerpt: Generally, a corporation is subject to the penalty if it did not timely pay at least the smaller of: the tax shown on its 2025 return, or the tax shown on its 2024 return (if it filed a 2024 return showing at least some amount of tax and the return was for a full 12 months). ... A large corporation is a corporation ... that had ... taxable income ... of $1 million or more for any of the 3 tax years immediately preceding the 2025 tax year ... The corporation is generally required to enter the 15th day of the 4th ... 6th, 9th, and 12th months of its tax year.
matchPhrases: generally, a corporation is subject to the penalty if it did not timely pay at least the smaller of: the tax shown on its 2025 return, or the tax shown on its 2024 return (if it filed a 2024 return showing at least some amount of tax and the return was for a full 12 months)
taxable income (defined below) of $1 million or more for any of the 3 tax years immediately preceding the 2025 tax year
the corporation is generally required to enter the 15th day of the 4th (form 990-pf filers, use the 5th month), 6th, 9th, and 12th months of its tax year
if an installment is due on a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday, payments made on the next day that is not a saturday, sunday, or legal holiday are considered made timely
rules.pageOrSection: Who Must Pay the Underpayment Penalty; Part II, line 8; Part III, lines 9 to 11
rules.ruleOrLimit: Required installment: 25% of the smaller of the current-year tax and the prior full-year tax; due April 15, June 15, September 15 and December 15.
rules.hangsApplication: The 2025 tax is $59,302.33 and the 2024 tax $48,300.00 (a 12-month return). HANGS is not a large corporation: its taxable income was $186,400.00, $211,900.00 and $230,000.00 in 2022 to 2024. Each installment was $12,075.00. June 15, 2025 was a Sunday, so June 16 was on time.
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Corporations

rules.question: How is the penalty for the short September installment figured?
rules.whyItMatters: The penalty runs from the installment's due date until the shortfall is paid; a later payment goes first to the earliest unpaid installment.
rules.excerpt: The period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year. ... A payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains.
matchPhrases: the period of underpayment generally runs from the installment due date to the earlier of the date the underpayment is actually paid or the 15th day of the 4th month after the close of the tax year
a payment of estimated tax is applied against unpaid required installments in the order in which installments are required to be paid, regardless of the installment to which the payment pertains
rules.ruleOrLimit: Penalty = underpayment x days x the underpayment rate, period by period.
rules.hangsApplication: The September 15 installment was $7,075.00 short. The $19,150.00 paid December 15 first made it up, then paid the fourth installment in full. The penalty runs 91 days, September 15 to December 15, 2025: $123.47, on line 34 (ESTTAX-01).
rules.unresolved: A person decides whether the annualized income installment method (Schedule A) would lower the penalty, and whether to attach Form 2220 or let the IRS bill it (ESTTAX-01).
rules.sourceTitle: Instructions for Form 2220 (2025), Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Corporations

rules.question: What underpayment rate applies to the September to December 2025 period?
rules.whyItMatters: Form 2220 prints the rate for each calendar quarter of the underpayment period.
rules.excerpt: Number of days on line 20 after 6/30/2025 and before 10/1/2025 ... x 7% (0.07) ... Number of days on line 20 after 9/30/2025 and before 1/1/2026 ... x 7% (0.07)
matchPhrases: number of days on line 20 after 6/30/2025 and before 10/1/2025
number of days on line 20 after 9/30/2025 and before 1/1/2026
rules.hangsApplication: 15 days in the July to September quarter ($7,075.00 x 15/365 x 7% = $20.35) and 76 days in the October to December quarter ($7,075.00 x 76/365 x 7% = $103.12).
rules.sourceTitle: Form 2220 (2025), Underpayment of Estimated Tax by Corporations

rules.question: Is the $120,000.00 advance to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC a loan, and does it carry imputed interest?
rules.whyItMatters: Juniper Ridge is owned by HANGS's Vice President, a 40% member. An advance without a note, interest or repayment terms may not be debt at all (it could be a distribution to that member), and a below-market loan between a corporation and its owners, directly or indirectly, can carry imputed interest.
rules.excerpt: (a) Treatment of gift loans and demand loans (1) In general. For purposes of this title, in the case of any below-market loan to which this section applies and which is a gift loan or a demand loan, the forgone interest shall be treated as ... (C) Corporation-shareholder loans. Any below-market loan directly or indirectly between a corporation and any shareholder of such corporation.
matchPhrases: in the case of any below-market loan to which this section applies and which is a gift loan or a demand loan, the forgone interest shall be treated as
corporation-shareholder loans any below-market loan directly or indirectly between a corporation and any shareholder of such corporation
rules.ruleOrLimit: Below-market loans between a corporation and its shareholders, directly or indirectly, may carry imputed interest; whether an advance is debt depends on the facts.
rules.hangsApplication: June 30, 2025: $120,000.00 wired to Juniper Ridge Partners LLC (owned by the Vice President, a 40% member), no note, no interest, no repayment date. The draft keeps it as a receivable on Schedule L line 6 and imputes no interest (RELATED-01).
rules.unresolved: A person decides whether the advance is bona fide debt (a signed note, a market rate, a repayment schedule) or a distribution, and whether section 7872 interest applies (RELATED-01).
rules.sourceTitle: 26 U.S. Code 7872, Treatment of loans with below-market interest rates

excluded.why: Washington has no corporate income tax; the business and occupation tax is a separate monthly filing.

HANGS's average gross receipts are far under the small business exemption; its $18,940.00 of equipment-note interest is deducted in full.
The $60,000.00 of dividends was reported on Forms 1099-DIV in January 2026 (Q11); not part of this return.
No section 179 election was made for 2025 (Q9).
